summary: Sumit Agarwal introduces Ario AI's mission: giving every person one real hour a day back by building a personal AI assistant for ordinary people, not just executives. The company announced raising $16 million. The system's foundation is "adversarial ETL"—the ability to extract users' personal data from major platforms (Google, Facebook, Amazon, DoorDash, Strava, Uber, Instagram, Twitter, and dozens of others) that don't want to make data export easy. Fewer than 1% of users have ever exported their data. On top of this aggregated data, Ario builds an agent architecture with LLM, RAG, and data management, packaged into use cases that add immediate value. Data privacy is emphasized: 100% of data belongs to the user, Ario takes no rights, data never leaves the user's device, and users have full CRUD access. After connecting data sources, Ario generates a "data portrait"—generative AI artwork reflecting the user's interests—along with a detailed auto-derived profile covering preferences, habits, and family details, with no intake form required. A memory component captures facts from conversations and explicit instructions. Agarwal demonstrates Ario against Copilot (travel recommendations) and ChatGPT (morning routine creation), showing personalized responses grounded in actual user data. He then shows school schedule photo upload with automatic calendar population and conflict detection, notifying users 24, 72, and 7 days in advance, with future email monitoring planned. Agarwal shares three RAG engineering principles: avoid the LLM at all costs by using cheap reliable tools first (illustrated with a Strava runtime subtraction example where the LLM struggled with trivial math); search is still king—abstract raw data into profiles rather than relying solely on vector embeddings; and present the right data at the right time to avoid overwhelming the pipeline. He introduces Aro boost, a browser extension offering two modes: login with Ario for mobile app integration, or offline developer mode where no account is created and downloaded data stays entirely local, usable with any LLM including Llama. Ario's mission to unlock user data power is a 20-year commitment. The company is hiring across all areas.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Mission
sections.summary: Agarwal expresses passion for generative AI and introduces Ario's mission to give every person one hour a day back. He quotes author Joanna about AI doing laundry so humans can be creative. Ario is building a personal assistant for ordinary people, not executives. He announces $16 million raised.

sections.title: Adversarial ETL and System Architecture
sections.summary: Agarwal introduces adversarial ETL as the foundation—extracting user data from platforms that don't want to share it. The system builds agent architecture with LLM and RAG on top of aggregated data. He notes fewer than 1% of users have ever exported their data. iOS app available for download.

sections.title: Data Privacy and Data Portrait
sections.summary: Agarwal emphasizes data belongs to user with full CRUD rights, data never moved. He acknowledges authentication friction. Shows co-founder Mong's data portrait—generative artwork reflecting photography, hiking, child interests. Auto-derived profile includes daycare appointments, restaurant preferences, Amazon purchases, and family medical needs. Profile is editable, requires no intake form.

sections.title: Memory Component and Profile Sources
sections.summary: Describes memory component capturing conversation-derived facts and explicit user instructions, claimed more robust than ChatGPT's memory. Profiles built from multiple data sources including Amazon, DoorDash, Twitter. Memory is separately editable.

sections.title: Demo: Travel Recommendations vs Copilot
sections.summary: Shows video demo comparing Copilot and Ario on travel query. Copilot gives generic 'Google Plus Plus' results. Ario recommends Maui (Asian food love), San Diego (Legoland, Lego toy purchases), Miami based on personal data. Envisions future queries incorporating schedule, budget, and multi-person harmonization.

sections.title: Demo: Morning Routine vs ChatGPT
sections.summary: Compares ChatGPT and Ario on morning routine query. ChatGPT exhibits '20 questions' failure mode. Ario produces personalized schedule tuned to actual wake-up time, exercise habits, and DoorDash food preferences. Mentions Gemini comparison skipped for time.

sections.title: School Schedule Management and Proactive Features
sections.summary: Agarwal demonstrates uploading a photo of a dense school schedule, which Ario extracts and publishes to the user's calendar. System identifies conflicts and notifies users 24, 72, and 7 days in advance. Addresses the common problem of schools not nailing down the first day of school—Ario holds duplicate entries until confirmed. A future feature (4-6 weeks out) will monitor email for scheduling updates and dynamically remove incorrect calendar entries. Broad email monitoring is not yet available; Ario special-cases one category at a time, starting with children's scheduling.

sections.title: RAG Engineering Insights
sections.summary: Agarwal shares three RAG principles. First: avoid the LLM at all costs—use cheap reliable traditional tools for data processing before resorting to LLMs. Illustrates with Strava runtime example where LLM declared the answer 'unknowable' but simple column subtraction yielded 55 minutes. Company principle: try 5-9 other approaches before using LLM. Second: search is still king—abstract raw data into processed profiles rather than relying solely on vector embeddings; only go to raw data when necessary. Third: present the right data at the right time; avoid putting too much data into pipeline to prevent system overwhelm. Team will publish blog posts and videos sharing lessons learned.

sections.title: Aro Boost Browser Extension
sections.summary: Introduces Aro boost, a browser extension usable in two modes: login with Ario for mobile app integration, or skip login for offline developer mode where no account is created. Developer mode downloads data from 15-20 sources to local device using screen scraping, APIs, and GDPR data downloads. Data stays entirely local—users can feed it to any LLM including Llama. Demo shows Suter Medical Health after-visit summaries being downloaded locally. Ario's mission to unlock user data power is a 20-year commitment.

sections.title: Closing
sections.summary: Agarwal thanks the audience, shares contact email, and notes the company is growing and hiring across all areas.
